```text
# #3481: Patch: run-sim reports dungeon runs act by act and can play them with curses, relics and a starting level
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The maintainer has a tool that plays whole dungeon runs with the AI to see how hard they are. Today it plays only the plainest run (level 1, no relics, no curses) and adds every act's fights together. So it cannot say whether act 3 is harder than act 1 (it is not: enemies do not get stronger), what a curse really costs, or whether dragging a fight out to rack up damage and healing earns more score than winning fast. After this change it can answer those questions, which is what tuning the placeholder enemies needs.

## Why

- §15.13's open questions include 'tuning the strawmen, against §15.12's `cargo jackioh run-sim`'.
- `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs:363-375`: every run starts with 'no artifact or curse, and the first level's unlocks'. `tally` (`:483`) groups fights by kind, and only the mini-bosses and the final boss are split by act.
- `crates/run/src/lib.rs:1054-1089` (`deal_map`): the act is known when each fight row is dealt but never reaches `fight_node`, and enemy health depends only on the kind of fight (`RUN_ENEMY_HEALTH`, `crates/run/src/config.rs:90`). An act-3 fight is an act-1 fight. With `RUN_ELITE_PERCENT` at 30 and rows of 2 or 3 nodes, the first fight row can be all elites.
- The score's damage, healing and cards-drawn terms are uncapped per fight (§15.10), so only a breakdown can show whether stalling pays.

## Proposal

- Add `--curses`, `--artifacts` and `--level N` to set a run's setup and unlocks, each refused when the content lacks what it names.
- The report gains a table per act (fights, win rate, HP cost, turns) and the score's breakdown (rows, wins, damage, healing, cards drawn, the boss and curse percents), mean and max.
- The run itself does not change: scaling enemies by act is the designer's call (§15.13), and this data informs it.
- Update the tools README row, which `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` holds to the CLI, and §15.12's measuring sentence.

## Where it lands

`crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs`, `crates/tools/README.md`, SPEC §15.12 (`spec/15-dungeon-run.md`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests: a tally of hand-built fight rows prints each act's row and the score breakdown, and a run set up with a curse, an artifact and a level folds to its end clean.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim` passes, and the daily sweep's ignored test still prints its report.
- [ ] An unknown curse or artifact id, or a level the content lacks, is refused with a message.
- [ ] The README row matches the CLI (the acceptance test).

## Size and risks

Medium, 3 files, tooling only. The defaults stay as they are today, so the daily sweep takes no longer.

_Written by `claude-4` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42630591699)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`cargo jackioh run-sim` gets three flags: `--curses ID,…`, `--artifacts ID,…` and `--level N`. They set every run's setup and unlocks. An unknown curse or artifact id, or a level the ladder lacks, is refused with a message before any fight is played.

The report gains two things. One is a table with a row per act (fights, won, win %, HP lost, turns). The other is the score's breakdown over the runs, mean and max: rows, wins, damage, healing, cards drawn, what the boss percents add and what the curse percent adds.

Defaults stay as today, so the daily sweep's output and speed do not change. `crates/run` does not change. The README row and §15.12's "Measuring it" sentence are updated.

## Files to touch

| File | Change | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs` | change | `Args` flags; new `Start`, `check_start`, `act_of`, `ScoreParts`, `score_parts`; `FightRow.act`; `Tally.acts` and `Tally.parts`; `render`; `run_setup`, `play_run`, `sweep` and `run` take the `Start`; module doc; tests |

## Steps

All edits are in `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs` unless said otherwise.

1. **Imports.**
   - `jackioh_run::config` also gives `RUN_SCORE_CARD_DRAWN, RUN_SCORE_DAMAGE, RUN_SCORE_FIGHT, RUN_SCORE_HEALING, RUN_SCORE_ROW, RUN_SLOT_LADDER`.
   - `jackioh_run` also gives `RunPassiveKind` and `run_check_setup`.
   - Beside `BOSSES`, add `const ACTS: usize = RUN_ACT_FIGHTS.len();`.

2. **`Args`.** Add, after `budget`:
   - `/// The curses every run starts with, by id. #[arg(long, value_delimiter = ',')] curses: Vec<String>`
   - `/// The artifacts every run starts with, by id; they count as unlocked. #[arg(long, value_delimiter = ',')] artifacts: Vec<String>`
   - `/// The starting deck's level, from 1 (1 by default). #[arg(long)] level: Option<usize>`
   - Use `Option` so no literal `1` appears in the CLI. The default is `RunUnlocks::default().level`.
   - Add no `value_parser` list. A possible-values list would have to be spelled out in the README row.

3. **`Start`, new.** Put it above `run_setup`.
   - Fields: `curses: Vec<String>`, `artifacts: Vec<String>`, `level: usize`.
   - Derive `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq`. Implement `Default` by hand: empty lists and `level: RunUnlocks::default().level`.
   - `fn from_args(args: &Args) -> Start` clones the lists and takes `args.level.unwrap_or(RunUnlocks::default().level)`.
   - `fn flags(&self) -> String` returns `""` for a default start. Otherwise it returns, in order and each only when set, `" --level {n}"` (only when it differs from the default), `" --curses a,b"` and `" --artifacts x,y"`.

4. **`run_setup(n, start: &Start)`.** Same seed and starter as today. `curses: start.curses.clone()`, `artifacts: start.artifacts.clone()`. Unlocks are `RunUnlocks { level: start.level, artifacts: start.artifacts.clone(), ..RunUnlocks::default() }`. `--artifacts` fills `unlocks.artifacts` so a relic that is not a starter can start the run; for a starter it is a no-op. Update the doc comment.

5. **`check_start(start: &Start, content: &RunContent) -> Result<(), String>`, new.** In this order:
   - Each curse id must be in `content.curses`. Otherwise return `format!("{id} is no curse; the content has {}", <ids joined ", ">)`.
   - Each artifact id must be a passive of kind `Combat` or `Economic`. Otherwise return `format!("{id} is no artifact a run may start with; the content has …")`, listing the ids of Combat or Economic passives that are not `unobtainable`. An Enemy or Blessing passive therefore counts as unknown.
   - `start.level` must be in `1..=RUN_SLOT_LADDER.len()`. Otherwise return `format!("there is no level {}: the levels are 1 to {}", …)`.
   - Then `let (setup, unlocks) = run_setup(0, start); run_check_setup(&setup, &unlocks, content)`. That reuses the run's own refusals: more than `RUN_STARTER_ARTIFACTS_MAX`, over `RUN_STARTER_ARTIFACT_POINTS`, Unobtainable, a duplicate artifact. Seed 0 is as valid as any `n`.
   - A curse named twice is not refused; the run accepts it (decision 4 under Open questions).

6. **`act_of(state: &RunState) -> usize`, new.**
   - It returns 0 when `state.row` is `None`. Otherwise it returns `state.map.iter().take(row).filter(|nodes| nodes.iter().any(|node| node.kind.is_boss())).count()`.
   - Only each act's last row holds a mini-boss or boss (`deal_map`, §15.5), so the boss rows before a row are the acts before it. A boss's own row is in its act.
   - This reads the map and duplicates no layout arithmetic.
   - Add a one-line doc comment.

7. **`FightRow`.** Add `act: usize`, documented "0-based, `act_of`'s". In `play_run`'s fight branch, inside the closure that builds the row, compute `act: act_of(&state)` beside `kind`.

8. **`play_run(n, content, start: &Start, fight, max_fights)`.** Replace `run_setup(n)` with `run_setup(n, start)`. Nothing else changes. Update its doc comment.

9. **`ScoreParts` and `score_parts(end, content)`, new.** Put them above `Tally`.
   - `ScoreParts` has `i64` fields `rows, wins, damage, healing, drawn, bosses, curses`. Derive `Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq`.
   - `fn terms(&self) -> [(&'static str, i64); 7]` gives these labels in order: `"rows"`, `"wins"`, `"damage"`, `"healing"`, `"cards drawn"`, `"boss percents"`, `"curse percent"`.
   - In `score_parts`, the first five terms are `run_score`'s own sums:
     - `rows` = `RUN_SCORE_ROW` × (`end.row` + 1, or 0 for none).
     - `wins` = `RUN_SCORE_FIGHT.of(kind)` × wins per kind. Plain wins are `fights_won - elites_won - ghosts_won - mini_bosses_won - bosses_won`, as `run_score` computes them.
     - `damage`, `healing` and `drawn` are `RUN_SCORE_DAMAGE`, `RUN_SCORE_HEALING` and `RUN_SCORE_CARD_DRAWN` × the `end.stats` fields.
   - The last two terms use `run_score` as the oracle, so the percent rules are not duplicated:
     - Let `base` be the sum of the first five terms.
     - Let `uncursed = run_score(&RunState { curses: Vec::new(), ..end.clone() }, content)`.
     - Then `bosses = uncursed - base` and `curses = run_score(end, content) - uncursed`.
     - The seven terms always sum to `run_score(end, content)`.

10. **`Tally`.**
    - Add `acts: [KindTally; ACTS]` ("by act, from the first") and `parts: Vec<ScoreParts>` ("each run's score by term").
    - Broaden `KindTally`'s doc comment to "one group of fights' sums (a kind's or an act's)". Keep the name.
    - In `tally`'s fight loop, add `if let Some(sums) = out.acts.get_mut(fight.act) { …same four += as the kind… }`. Share a small helper if that is shorter; an out-of-range act is skipped, as an unknown kind is.
    - Per run, add `out.parts.push(score_parts(&outcome.end, content))`.
    - Leave `boss_hp` as it is.

11. **`render`.**
    - Factor the kind table's two `format!`s into `fn table_header(first: &str) -> String` and `fn table_line(name: &str, sums: &KindTally) -> String`. Keep the exact widths `{:<10}{:>8}{:>6}{:>7}{:>9}{:>7}`, so the kind table prints byte for byte as before.
    - After the kind rows, push `'\n'`, `table_header("act")`, then one `table_line(&(at + 1).to_string(), sums)` per act. Then the existing "(HP lost is …)" note, which now covers both tables.
    - After `runs won:` and before `score:`, print for each of the seven labels `score from {label}: {mean_and_max(values)}`. Take the labels from `ScoreParts::default().terms()`. Take the values from `self.parts.iter().map(|p| p.terms()[at].1)`.
    - Keep the `score:` and `Embers:` lines unchanged.

12. **`sweep(seeds, from, skills, budget, start: &Start, content)`.**
    - Pass `start` to `play_run`.
    - Append `start.flags()` to `again`'s text, after `--budget {budget}`, so a fault's replay command is exact.
    - Append `start.flags()` to the header (`…, skill {skill}{flags}`). A default start prints today's header.

13. **`run(args)`.**
    - Before the skills default, build `let start = Start::from_args(&args);`.
    - After `run_catalog_content`, call `check_start(&start, &content).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("run-sim: {e}"))?;`. This is before `sweep`, so a bad id exits 1 with the message and plays nothing.
    - Pass `&start` to `sweep`.

14. **Module doc (top of the file).**
    - Say run `n` starts from the seed, the first `RUN_STARTER_SIZE` starting cards, the `--curses`, the `--artifacts` (which count as unlocked) and `--level` (none, none and level 1 by default).
    - Say the report prints the act table and the score's breakdown.
    - Add example lines: `cargo jackioh run-sim --seeds 4 --curses temp-curse-2 --artifacts temp-thick-skin --level 3`.
    - Say today's level changes only the slot check, since the starting cards are Commons and Rares. The first ten are 7 Commons and 3 Rares and fit every level.

15. **`crates/tools/README.md`, line 17's `run-sim` row.**
    - First-cell code span: `run-sim --seeds N [--from N] [--skill S,…] [--budget tiny\|full] [--curses ID,…] [--artifacts ID,…] [--level N]`. Keep the `\|` escape. The acceptance test reads the spans and needs every clap flag named.
    - Prose: replace "with the first starting cards and no artifact or curse" with "with the first starting cards and, unless `--curses`, `--artifacts` and `--level` set them, no artifact or curse and level 1 (each id is refused when the content lacks it, `--artifacts` also unlocks the relics it names, a level past `RUN_SLOT_LADDER` is refused, and today a level only gates the starting deck's slot check)".
    - Printed list: replace "a table of each kind of fight's … turns, then" with "a table of each kind of fight's … turns and one of each act's, then"; replace "the score and the Embers" with "the score's breakdown (the mean and max of each term: rows, wins, damage, healing, cards drawn and what the boss percents and the curse percent add), the score and the Embers".
    - Name #3481.

16. **`spec/15-dungeon-run.md`, §15.12 "Measuring it".** Replace the sentence with: "`cargo jackioh run-sim` plays seeded whole runs with the AI in the player's seat at [[R747000]]'s skill, from level 1 with no artifact or curse unless `--level`, `--artifacts` and `--curses` set them (each refused when the content lacks it), and prints each kind of fight's and each act's win rate, HP cost and turns, the HP at each boss, the rows reached, the score by term (rows, wins, damage, healing, cards drawn, and what the boss percents and the curse percent add) and the Embers (#3065, #3481): a guide to tuning the strawmen, not a target." Do not touch the constants table.

17. **Existing tests.** Pass `&Start::default()`: `run_setup(0)` becomes `run_setup(0, &Start::default())` (3 places). `play_run(...)` gets `&Start::default()` as its third argument (2 places). `sweep(...)` gets it before `&content` (1 place). Change the `row(...)` helper to set `act: 0`.

## Tests

All are in `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs`'s `mod tests`. Derive ids from `content()` (first curse, first `Combat` passive with `starter && !unobtainable`), not from placeholder literals, so the designer's lists do not break them.

- `the_act_is_the_count_of_boss_rows_before_a_row`.
  - Build run 0 and set `row: Some(r)` on a clone of its state for every row of `map`.
  - Assert `act_of` equals the act computed independently from §15.5: act `a` spans `2 * RUN_ACT_FIGHTS[a] + 1` rows.
  - Assert `map.len()` is the sum of those spans.
  - Assert each act's last row is one node with `kind.is_boss()`.
- `a_run_with_a_curse_an_artifact_and_a_level_folds_to_its_end`.
  - Use stub won fights, as `the_policy_walks…` does.
  - `Start { curses: [curse], artifacts: [artifact], level: 3 }`, three seeds.
  - Assert no faults and `end.phase == Won`.
  - Assert `run_fold(&file, &content) == Ok(end)`.
  - Assert `file.setup.curses`, `file.unlocks.level == 3` and `file.unlocks.artifacts` are as set.
  - Assert `end.curses == [curse]` and `run_curse_points(&end, &content) > 0`. Import `run_curse_points` in the test module.
  - Assert the artifact is held.
  - Assert the fights split by `act` as `RUN_ACT_FIGHTS[a] + 1` each.
- `a_cursed_runs_first_fight_ends_clean`.
  - Same start, real `play_fight` at `TEST_BUDGET`, `max_fights: Some(1)`, as the existing first test does.
  - Assert no faults and `run_fold(&file, &content) == Ok(end)`.
- `check_start_refuses_what_the_content_lacks`.
  - An unknown curse id gives an `Err` containing the id.
  - An unknown artifact id and `looming-presence` (an Enemy passive) give an `Err` containing the id.
  - Levels 0 and `RUN_SLOT_LADDER.len() + 1` give an `Err` containing the level.
  - `RUN_STARTER_ARTIFACTS_MAX + 1` distinct Combat or Economic obtainable artifacts give an `Err`.
  - `Start::default()` is `Ok`.
  - Every level `1..=RUN_SLOT_LADDER.len()` is `Ok`.
  - A non-starter, obtainable artifact with `run_artifact_points(&content, id) <= RUN_STARTER_ARTIFACT_POINTS` is `Ok`, and `run_setup` puts it in `unlocks.artifacts`.
- `the_tally_splits_the_fights_by_act_and_the_score_by_term`.
  - Add a helper `fn in_act(act: usize, row: FightRow) -> FightRow`.
  - Hand-built fights: act 0 has Fight 30→25 won turns 10, Elite 25→0 lost turns 14, Fight 30→30 won turns 8 and MiniBoss 30→20 won turns 20. Act 1 has Fight 20→18 won turns 6, Ghost 18→18 won turns 10 and MiniBoss 18→10 won turns 16.
  - Assert `sums.acts[0]` is `{4, 3, 40, 52}` and `sums.acts[1]` is `{3, 3, 10, 32}`.
  - Assert `sums.acts[2]` is default.
  - Assert the rendered act rows' words, found by first word as the existing test does: `["1","4","3","75.0","10.0","13.0"]`, `["2","3","3","100.0","3.3","10.7"]`, and a line `3` ending in `-`.
  - One end state has `stats` with no boss wins and no curses. Assert `score_parts(..)` has `bosses == 0 && curses == 0`, and `rows + wins + damage + healing + drawn == run_score`. This is the drift guard on the five direct terms.
  - Another end state has `mini_bosses_won: 1`, `bosses_won: 1` and a curse. Assert `bosses > 0 && curses > 0` and the seven terms sum to `run_score`.
  - Assert that `render`'s text contains `score from rows: ` followed by `mean_and_max` of the two runs' `rows` terms, and the other six labels' lines.

Commands, all run from the repository root:
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim -- --ignored --nocapture` (the daily sweep still prints its report; slow, so run it once at the end)
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance readme_`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance dungeon_`
- `cargo run -p jackioh-tools -- run-sim --seeds 1 --budget tiny --curses nope` exits 1 naming `nope`. Do the same with `--artifacts nope` and `--level 9`.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo jackioh spec check`

## Done when

- [ ] `--curses`, `--artifacts` and `--level` set each run's setup and unlocks, and `--artifacts` also unlocks the relics it names.
- [ ] An unknown curse or artifact id, or a level outside the ladder, is refused with a message before any fight is played. The run's own refusals (too many relics, too many points) come through the same way.
- [ ] The report prints the per-act table and the score breakdown, with mean and max.
- [ ] Default output is unchanged apart from the new lines; the kind table prints byte for byte as before.
- [ ] A fault's "again" command and the header carry the new flags.
- [ ] README row and §15.12 are updated; the acceptance README test passes.
- [ ] The new unit tests and `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim` pass, and the ignored daily sweep still prints its report.
- [ ] rustfmt, clippy and `spec check` are clean; no file outside the three is changed.

## Risks

- **Drift from `run_score`.**
  - The five direct terms copy `run_score`'s arithmetic. The guard test (no boss wins, no curse, parts equal the score) fails if a term is added or changed.
  - The percent terms come from `run_score` itself, so they cannot drift.
- **Act from the map, not arithmetic.** If `deal_map` ever puts a boss node in another row, `act_of` still follows the map, and the independent §15.5 test fails and says so.
- **README acceptance test.**
  - Every clap flag must appear in the row's first-cell code span, and `\|` must stay escaped.
  - Do not add possible values, or they must be spelled in the row.
  - Run it after the README edit.
- **Determinism.**
  - The policy stream, seeds and rayon ordering are untouched.
  - New state is read-only: tallies from `end` and the fight rows.
  - Run order stays seed order.
- **Purity.** Everything lives in `crates/tools`, which may use the disk and clock. Nothing is added to the pure crates, and the tools' `Cargo.toml` is unchanged.
- **Real fights under a curse.** `play_fight` already runs `validate_setup`, and the fuzz covers run-style handicaps (#3283). If the cursed real-fight test throws, report it. Do not skip it.
- **No game rules changed.** `Start` only fills `RunSetup` and `RunUnlocks` the run already checks.

## Open questions

None blocks the build. The decisions below are taken; a person may overrule any:

1. **`--level` effect.** It only sets `unlocks.level`, which `run_check_setup` reads for the slot check, so today it changes nothing the run plays: every starting card is Common or Rare and the first ten fit every level. Rejected: picking a level-aware starting deck (more Rares at higher levels). That would change what the starter deck is, so it is a design call and not this issue's.
2. **Artifacts are unlocked automatically.** `--artifacts` also fills `unlocks.artifacts`. Rejected: refusing non-starter relics, which would block measuring most of the placeholders.
3. **Act and score terms are computed in the tool.** Rejected: a public `run_act` or `run_score_parts` in `crates/run`, which the issue rules out ("the run itself does not change") and which would touch a pure crate and its README.
4. **Duplicate curses.** A curse named twice is accepted, as the run accepts it. Say so if the designer wants stacking refused.
5. **Whether a per-act table should also split kinds within acts.** Not built; one row per act, as the issue's tests describe.
```

- [ ] `--curses`, `--artifacts` and `--level` set each run's setup and unlocks, and `--artifacts` also unlocks the relics it names.

- [ ] The new unit tests and `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim` pass, and the ignored daily sweep still prints its report.
- [ ] rustfmt, clippy and `spec check` are clean; no file outside the three is changed.

## Risks

- **Drift from `run_score`.**
  - The five direct terms copy `run_score`'s arithmetic. The guard test (no boss wins, no curse, parts equal the score) fails if a term is added or changed.
  - The percent terms come from `run_score` itself, so they cannot drift.
- **Act from the map, not arithmetic.** If `deal_map` ever puts a boss node in another row, `act_of` still follows the map, and the independent §15.5 test fails and says so.
- **README acceptance test.**
  - Every clap flag must appear in the row's first-cell code span, and `\|` must stay escaped.
  - Do not add possible values, or they must be spelled in the row.
  - Run it after the README edit.
- **Determinism.**
  - The policy stream, seeds and rayon ordering are untouched.
  - New state is read-only: tallies from `end` and the fight rows.
  - Run order stays seed order.
- **Purity.** Everything lives in `crates/tools`, which may use the disk and clock. Nothing is added to the pure crates, and the tools' `Cargo.toml` is unchanged.
- **Real fights under a curse.** `play_fight` already runs `validate_setup`, and the fuzz covers run-style handicaps (#3283). If the cursed real-fight test throws, report it. Do not skip it.
- **No game rules changed.** `Start` only fills `RunSetup` and `RunUnlocks` the run already checks.

## Open questions

None blocks the build. The decisions below are taken; a person may overrule any:

1. **`--level` effect.** It only sets `unlocks.level`, which `run_check_setup` reads for the slot check, so today it changes nothing the run plays: every starting card is Common or Rare and the first ten fit every level. Rejected: picking a level-aware starting deck (more Rares at higher levels). That would change what the starter deck is, so it is a design call and not this issue's.
2. **Artifacts are unlocked automatically.** `--artifacts` also fills `unlocks.artifacts`. Rejected: refusing non-starter relics, which would block measuring most of the placeholders.
3. **Act and score terms are computed in the tool.** Rejected: a public `run_act` or `run_score_parts` in `crates/run`, which the issue rules out ("the run itself does not change") and which would touch a pure crate and its README.
4. **Duplicate curses.** A curse named twice is accepted, as the run accepts it. Say so if the designer wants stacking refused.
5. **Whether a per-act table should also split kinds within acts.** Not built; one row per act, as the issue's tests describe.
